could_not_do: COULD NOT USE F2's material_showcase FIXTURE for this piece's primary instrument. Surveyed it first (do not repeat the survey): the wall's front face normal is (0,0,1) and in sky.js's apply(), dir.y (elevation) and dir.z share a sign at every daylight hour (azim==ang exactly, and elev=sin(azim), dir.z=sin(azim)*0.75), so dot(N,sunDir) > 0 for the whole day and the wall front never receives a camera-visible cast shadow. This is a real, load-bearing property of the sky model, not a guess -- worth flagging for anyone else who reaches for this fixture expecting a directional-shadow test. Moved to the VP04-settlement-street pose (town-thorn, real production content, matches F2's own production-thorn evidence camera) at 09:00, which does show genuine cast-shadow structure.

MY FIRST NULL-CONTROL METRIC (falloff_ratio = p90/p10 of the whole crop) WAS THE WRONG OPERATIONALISATION OF 'DIRECTIONAL FALLOFF', FOUND BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY REASONING IN ADVANCE. Measured on real hardware-adjacent (SwiftShader) captures: a flat additive lift K, solved to match my real fix's shadow-floor lift exactly, produced a HIGHER falloff_ratio than the real fix (4.00 vs 3.46 at the first tuning). Diagnosis: the ratio rewards moving p90 (the lit end) up right alongside p10, which is the flattening a global lift does, not evidence against it -- my real fix correctly leaves p90 almost untouched (+0.36 out of 55, <1%) while the null control moves it by +K (+12, ~22%) by construction, and that p90 stability is what actually says 'this did not flatten the lighting'. Replaced the gating check with a direct p90-movement comparison between the two arms at matched p10 (GI-MOVES-THE-LIT-END-FAR-LESS-THAN-A-MATCHED-GLOBAL-LIFT) and kept falloff_ratio as reported, non-gating context. Recorded here because RULES rule 4 asks a probe capable of failing to be shown failing, and this is that evidence for the TOOL, not just the shader.

TUNING: the first uGIStrength (0.55, uGIRadius 1.6m, uGIMaxDist 0.6m) raised the production crop's p10_luma from 4.7 to 16.0 -- a large, tonemap-amplified jump that also measurably reduced local_contrast_med (6.28 -> 4.01, ~36%), i.e. some genuine loss of fine texture contrast alongside the shadow-floor lift (the bounce-average is, mechanically, a soft blur of nearby lit colour, and averaging too wide a neighbourhood into a very dark pixel can wash out what little texture the base shading carried). Reducing uGIStrength to 0.22 (radius 1.0m, maxDist 0.4m) barely moved the outcome (p10 15.1, local_contrast_med 4.37) -- the tonemap's response near black is not linear in the HDR delta, so this axis is not a simple proportional knob. Shipped at the lower (0.22/1.0/0.4) tuning since it is strictly better on local_contrast_med with no measured cost, but the local_contrast_med regression is NOT eliminated at this tuning and is named here rather than hidden. A shader that separated 'how much to lift' from 'how much to blur' (e.g. capping the sample count or weighting more sharply toward the nearest, most reliable taps) would likely do better and is out of scope for this pass -- named as owed below.
NO HARDWARE GPU EVIDENCE YET -- all measurement so far is SwiftShader (software_renderer=true). Owed before landing, matching F2's own three-attempt pattern; recorded as next_step.
